_note: Monte Carlo companion for the transimpedance stage. Contributes fragments only;
the master file and the corner fragments come from anatop_tb_tia.json.
block is TiaAmpMC, NOT TiaAmp -- the block name keys data/raw/corners_<Block>.json
and data/extract_<Block>.ocn, which the configs would otherwise clobber.
The two tests are NOT two Maestro tests. Maestro writes one mcdata per test
containing every design point pooled, so the 35k and 560k gain taps land in one
file and maestro2tex would average them together into nonsense. scratchpad/
split_mc.py splits them into TiaFbTB35k__mc.csv / TiaFbTB560k__mc.csv and drops
the 48 of 400 samples that did not converge. Render with --no-extract; there is
no live run to extract from and the CSVs are self-describing.
PUBLISHABLE OUTPUTS ONLY. Every DC-sweep-derived output (gain_err, inl_lsb,
tue_lsb, f3db, x_src_lim) is deliberately absent: they degrade on the same
samples as the 48 non-converged ones and are under investigation. Do not add

figures.caption: Transimpedance loop phase margin at maximum gain over 179 converged samples of 200 (process and mismatch), \SI{37}{\celsius}. Every converged sample clears the \SI{45}{\degree} floor, the worst at \SI{46.6}{\degree}, which is what validates $C_f = \SI{22}{\pico\farad}$ --- the corner run behind Table~\ref{tab:tia-cl-stability} gave \SIrange{61.2}{64.9}{\degree} and carries no mismatch at all. The distribution is right-skewed, so \(p_1\)/\(p_{99}\) and worst case are quoted rather than mean \(\pm\,3\sigma\). 48 of 400 samples did not converge and are excluded (Section~\ref{sss:tia-mc}).

Closed-loop gain peaking at maximum gain, same 179 samples. \SI{87.7}{\percent} sit below the \SI{2}{\decibel} criterion, worst case \SI{2.61}{\decibel}. Peaking fails before phase margin does because it responds to the same mismatch with less headroom against its limit; at $R_f = \SI{35}{\kilo\ohm}$ it is identically zero across every sample.

Input offset at maximum gain, 179 converged samples of 200 (process and mismatch). \(\sigma = \SI{7.09}{\milli\volt}\) against a \(\pm\SI{5}{\milli\volt}\) budget gives \SI{54.7}{\percent} per-channel yield and, over four identical channels, roughly \SI{9}{\percent} of chips with all four in budget. This is the block's binding limitation and it is a mismatch quantity, so no corner run bounds it. The control amplifier fails the same way (Section~\ref{ss:controlamp}).

tables.caption: Monte Carlo stability at minimum gain, $R_f = \SI{35}{\kilo\ohm}$. \textbf{Process and mismatch} (\texttt{castalia\_pm\_25}), \SI{37}{\celsius}, 200 samples, seed 12345, LDS sampling, $C_f = \SI{22}{\pico\farad}$, electrode \texttt{randles\_cell} with $R_s = \SI{100}{\ohm}$, $R_{\mathrm{ct}} = \SI{1}{\mega\ohm}$, $C_{\mathrm{dl}} = \SI{100}{\nano\farad}$. The \(N\) column is the converged sample count: 27 of 200 did not converge and are excluded, for the reason given in Section~\ref{sss:tia-mc}. \(\sigma\) here is die-to-die and channel-to-channel combined; it is not comparable with a mismatch-only \(\sigma\).

Monte Carlo stability at maximum gain, $R_f = \SI{560}{\kilo\ohm}$, conditions otherwise as Table~\ref{tab:tia-mc-stab35k}. This is the binding gain setting: phase margin still clears the \SI{45}{\degree} floor on every converged sample, but peaking passes on only \SI{87.7}{\percent}. 21 of 200 samples did not converge and are excluded.

Monte Carlo offset and input-referred noise at maximum gain, conditions as Table~\ref{tab:tia-mc-stab560k}. Offset is close to Gaussian, so mean \(\pm\,3\sigma\) is meaningful here; it is not quoted for the skewed stability quantities. At $R_f = \SI{35}{\kilo\ohm}$ the same measurement gives \(\sigma = \SI{4.68}{\milli\volt}\) and \SI{74.0}{\percent} yield, so offset degrades with gain because the electrode's DC noise gain multiplies it. The four-channel column assumes the four channels are independent draws, which a process-and-mismatch run overstates --- a \texttt{castalia\_mm\_25} re-run would separate die-to-die from within-die.
